svg.text: Dashboard & Aggregation — The Live Path vs. Two Layers of Dead Strategy Code
Smart Credit Solution Enterprises Admin Portal
⚠ CRITICAL — DashboardController has zero access control
@RequestMapping("/api/dashboard") — 4 endpoints, none call HierarchyAccessService or HierarchyAccessValidator
POST /get · GET /wallet-balance/{hierarchyId} · GET /profile/{hierarchyId} · POST /data
Every method takes hierarchyId directly (path variable or request body) and passes it straight into
DashboardServiceImpl with no check that it belongs to, or is a descendant of, the caller's own identity.
A classic IDOR — any authenticated user, at any level, can view any OTHER hierarchy's wallet balance and profile
by ID alone — no token spoofing required. This is distinct from, and compounds, the Module 4 identity-spoofing bug.
⚠ Confirmed bug: Enterprises profile lookup is broken
DashboardServiceImpl.getUserProfile(hierarchyId) switches on commonMethods.extractHierarchyType(hierarchyId):
case "EN" -> enterprisesRepository.findByEnterpriseId(...) // real Enterprises IDs extract to type "ET", never "EN"
default -> throw new RuntimeException("Unsupported hierarchy type: " + type)
Per Module 2/1, HierarchyMaster seeds the code "ET" for Enterprises — not "EN". Every real Enterprises hierarchyId falls
through to default and throws "Unsupported hierarchy type: ET" — this endpoint is broken for the entire ET level.
Two dead layers of the intended strategy pattern
Layer 1 — DashboardStrategy (buildDashboard)
• ADDashboardStrategy — stub, returns Map.of() unconditionally
• RtDashboardStrategy — full, real implementation (150 lines):
balances, last-5 transactions, aggregation cards
• SdDashboardStrategy — full, real implementation (129 lines),
same shape for SuperDistributor
Confirmed by search: referenced by NOTHING outside their
own 4 files. No controller, no service ever selects one.
Two real, working implementations sit completely unused.
Layer 2 — HierarchyAggregationStrategy
Exactly ONE implementation: HierarchyAggregationStrategyImpl
— a plain @Service, no name or @Qualifier given.
Map<String, HierarchyAggregationStrategy> strategies
is keyed by Spring bean NAME, not hierarchy code —
so strategies.get("RT") / .get("SD") / .get(anything)
always returns null → getStrategy() always throws
IllegalArgumentException, for every type, no exceptions.
If Layer 1 were ever wired up, it would break here immediately
— RtDashboardStrategy calls getStrategy("RT") directly.
Even setting the keying bug aside: HierarchyAggregationStrategyImpl.getTransactionVolume() and .getServicePieData()/.getLast4MonthsGraphData() are themselves stubs returning null/empty.
The live path — DashboardServiceImpl (2,416 lines)
DashboardController → DashboardService → DashboardServiceImpl (the actual, working dashboard)
Switches on hierarchy type internally
commonMethods.extractHierarchyType() called 4×
inside this one class — its own type-branching,
independent of both dead strategy layers above.
Its own recursive subtree walk
userDetailsRepository.findByParentAccount(), walked
recursively — rather than the AccessHierarchyPath
closure table built for exactly this in Module 2.
